analysis.changeIsolation: Replacing only the ReadObject mutable reference and two moves with the pinned baseline conversion reproduces the exact supplied baseline SHA. All error/not-found paths, maximum-int check, validation expressions/order, Call/callback/wait logic and WriteObject remain byte-identical.
analysis.ownershipAndLifetime: Service::Response is base::expected<ProviderResponse, ProviderFailure>, not a borrowed provider response. ResponseCallback is base::OnceCallback<void(Response)>. Respond accepts ProviderResponse by value, builds an owned Response, removes the pending callback and invokes it with std::move(result). The UI callback emplaces its owned response then signals ready. Successful TimedWait precedes the engine move out of Reply. Call returns the response by value to ReadObject. Reply is refcounted and retained by callback/tasks across timeout or cancellation; abandoned branches do not read response. Moving fields after Call therefore neither borrows callback storage nor changes concurrent access. No further response/success/data/revision reads occur after constructing the return object.
analysis.typesAndConstness: api.patch declares optional success, ArrayBuffer data and DOMString revision. Local service code treats data as an owning byte container and uses std::vector<uint8_t> in WriteObject; vault-transport.patch explicitly defines output fields as std::vector<uint8_t> and std::string. Mutable local response -> mutable success -> mutable optional payloads permits actual moves. The source change removes const from the ReadObject reference. A separate const-move control compiled the actual conversion with const restored and still observed 9 allocations and zero data transfers, so merely spelling std::move is not accepted as ownership evidence. Generated API C++ fields and base::expected overloads were not compiled or directly verified by this model.
analysis.validationAndMovedValues: Checks for engaged data/revision, nonempty revision and maximum size are unchanged and precede both moves. Aggregate list initialization moves two distinct owned fields in order; no expression depends on either moved-from value. Owned return vector/string outlive the response. No-data, no-revision, empty-revision and oversize rejection cases pass; empty data remains accepted by this conversion as before, while actual service ValidateSuccessResponse additionally rejects empty object data and validates revision syntax.
analysis.modelEvidence: The diagnostic compiles the extracted conversion text with optional/variant wrappers and model structs, not the actual expected/optional result chain or generated headers. It asserts returned values after response destruction and observes original vector storage transfer for four nonempty cases. Long revisions force a copy allocation in the baseline. The exact source/baseline SHA gates prevent silently testing a different conversion. It does not exercise service callbacks, synchronization, cancellation or native API build compatibility. Allocation counts describe the fixture, with no physical RAM, CPU or browser performance claim.
analysis.packetAndMigration: Packet regeneration and checksum comparison reproduce 9 extension resources, 1 native source and 11 host modules, with 29 checksum entries total. Exact native mapping is native-provider-transport.cc -> chrome/browser/sync/breezer_sync/provider_transport.cc. The allowlisted set rejects extra/missing resource entries. Preflight reads and hashes replacement bytes, verifies every current source and existing sourceChanges after pin is either before or after, and retains captured replacement bytes before any backup/resource/plan write. Each file uses temp-write/fsync/rename. Source writes precede the combined plan write; both before and after are accepted to resume source-before-pin interruptions. Already-after sources retain mtimes. Existing sourceChanges records and unrelated plan fields are preserved; graph/output/cache files are not targets. Packet host modules are staged separately and never migrated into Chromium.
analysis.testAdequacy: Migration tests cover native packet/source/pin rejection before writes, interrupted native-source-before-pin recovery, full interrupted migration recovery, repeat mtimes/backups, unchanged cache sentinel, and packet mutation after preflight. Packaging tests cover matching and stale host files, incomplete/unknown receipts, corrupt packet and symlink rejection. Native conversion tests meaningfully cover local conversion ownership and validation, with independently reproduced baseline and constness controls. Broader generated-header, callback/concurrency and Windows/WSL launch acceptance are outside these tests.
